newsitem.title: USA: Writer of Presley's "Heartbreak Hotel" dies at 82.
newsitem.headline: Writer of Presley's "Heartbreak Hotel" dies at 82.

text.p: Mae Boren Axton, co-writer of "Heartbreak Hotel," the hit that catapulted Elvis Presley to stardom in 1956, was found dead on Wednesday at her home, a medical official said.
She was 82 and had been in ill health, according to medical examiner Dr. Charles Harlan.
Axton, a songwriter and promoter of musical acts, entered rock'n'roll history in 1955 when she co-wrote "Heartbreak Hotel" with a friend, Tommy Durden.
Inspired by a newspaper article about a man who left a suicide note with the line "I walk a lonely street," the pair scribbled out some lyrics and got the song on tape within 22 minutes.

They played a rough cut to the up-and-coming Presley, who loved the song but loathed the title. Released in January 1956 as his first single for RCA Records, it catapulted him into the national spotlight and went on to top the charts around the world. It was the year's best-selling single in the U.S., according to Billboard magazine.
Chet Atkins played rhythm guitar on the recording, which won a 1995 award in the Grammy "Hall of Fame", set up to honour early recordings of lasting significance.

Axton, who was also instrumental in furthering the careers of Willie Nelson and Dolly Parton, joined other celebrities just last Monday paying tribute to Merle Haggard on his 60th birthday at the "Nashville Nightlife" club. She presented Haggard with personal framed photos of Minnie Pearl, Ernest Tubb and other "old timers" dating from Axton's early years in country music.

She is survived by a son, Hoyt Axton, a noted singwriter in his own right. His credits include Steppenwolf's "The Pusher," Three Dog Night's "Joy to the World" and the Kingston Trio's "Greenback Dollar."
